name: Frontend Application
description: The production React/Vite SPA in Rolliude-front, including pages, routing, UI components, design tokens/styles, and its build/runtime config; also contains the disconnected legacy login.html entry point kept alongside the canonical index.html.

name: Backend API (Canonical)
description: The current Express/Prisma backend built under the modular src/modules/<domain> pattern, with app bootstrap, config, shared error handling, middleware, and its own build config, representing the actual source of truth for auth and user endpoints.

name: Backend Legacy / Dead Code
description: Duplicate flat src/{controllers,routes,schemas,services}/ and src/server.ts files left over from before the migration to src/modules/<domain>, functionally superseded by the canonical backend layer and candidates for removal.

name: Data Layer
description: The Prisma schema, its generated migration (tables for usuarios, password_reset_tokens, estados, municipios, generos, filmes), the migration lock file, and the loose root-level usuarios.sql reference dump.

name: Infrastructure & CI/CD
description: Container definitions for both apps, the root docker-compose orchestration, Dockerfile build steps, and the GitHub Actions quality-check pipeline with its frontend/backend jobs.

name: Project Governance & Standards
description: Rolliude-project's ADRs, authority map and per-area standard files that are the canonical source of truth for architecture decisions, plus the repo-level agent instructions skill and the quality-check script that enforces these rules.

name: Root Config & Docs
description: Monorepo-wide shared configuration (nvm, prettier, root package.json/tsconfig, env example), top-level README/AGENTS instructions, the stray root database.ts helper, and GitHub issue/PR templates.

name: Disconnected Signup Prototype
description: The standalone 'rolliúde-play tela cadastro' Vite+React app with its own login/register UI, mock region data, and build config — not imported by or wired into Rolliude-front, and architecturally isolated from the rest of the platform.
